questions.question: What is the intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj Institutions called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Panchayat Samiti.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Panchayat Samiti **is the** intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj Institutions.**
 
• It is the** tehsil or taluka or block level of the rural local-self government system** in India.
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the block level is an Administrative Authority that is responsible for enforcing the law and carrying it into effect.
 
• They form the middle level of the Panchayati Raj Institutions in India.
 
• It acts as a link between Village Panchayats (Gram Panchayats) and Zila Parishad (District council).
 
• It was formalized in 1992 by the 73rd amendment to the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Panchayati Raj

 
 
• Panchayati Raj is the system of local self-government of villages in rural India as opposed to urban and suburban municipalities.
 
• It consists of the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through which the self-government of villages is realized.
 
• They are tasked with "economic development, strengthening social justice and implementation of Central and State Government Schemes including those 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule."
 
• ​Part IX of the Indian Constitution is the section of the Constitution relating to the Panchayats.
 
• It stipulates that in states or Union Territories with more than two million inhabitants there are three levels of PRIs:
 
 
• Zilla Parishad at the District Level
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the Block Level
 
• Gram/Village Panchayat at the Village Level

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a synovial joint in the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sutures joint.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The sutures joint is NOT a synovial joint in the human body.**
 
• The immovable joints between the plates of the skull are known as sutures joints.
 
• The bones of the skull are an example.
 
• An immovable joint is an articulation between bones in which no movement occurs.
 
• It is also called a synarthrosis joint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The hinge joint:**

 
 
• It is commonly referred to as the knee.
 
• Hinge Joint is a joint in the human body that serves motion in one plane.
 
• It is a common class of synovial joint that includes the:-
 
 
• Ankle.
 
• Knee.
 
• Finger Joints.
 
• Toe Joints.
 
 
 
• They are made up of two or more bones with articular surfaces that are covered by hyaline cartilage and lubricated by synovial liquid.
 
 
 
• **Ball and Socket Joint:-**
 
 
• These joints are a type of synovial joint where the spheroid articular surface of one bone sits within a cup-like depression of another bone.
 
• These joints include:-
 
 
• Glenohumeral Joint.
 
• Hip Joint

questions.question: As on July 2020, employees whose monthly wages are ______ or below are covered under the ESI Act.
questions.solution:

• **As of July 2020, employees whose monthly wages are Rs.21000 or below are covered under the ESI Act.**
 
• **Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948:**
 
 
• **The ESI Act 1948** was the first major legislation on social security for workers in India.
 
• Under the Act, employers and employees contribute their share, respectively, with the rate of contribution being decided through the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
 
• It applies to premises where 10 or more persons are employed.
 
• Employees with wages up to **Rs. 21,000 a month (earlier Rs. 15,000 per month) are entitled to the health insurance cover and other benefits under the ESI Act.**
 
• ESI Corporation (ESIC), which is an autonomous body, regulates medical services being provided by the ESI Scheme in the respective states and Union Territories.
 
• The scheme was inaugurated in** Kanpur on 24th February 1952.**

questions.question: Which country launched the first artificial satellite Sputnik 1?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__USSR.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **On October 4, 1957, the Soviet Union/USSR sent the first artificial satellite 'Sputnik-1' into space.**
 
• The satellite was able to complete the orbiter of the** Earth in 96.2 minutes at a speed of 29000 kilometres per hour**.
 
• At the time of launch, it weighed around** 83.6 kg. Its diameter was 58 cm.**
 
• Sputnik was made like a metal ball and had four antennas.
 
• Sputnik-1 was giving signals of **20.005 and 40.002 MHz.**
 
• Sputnik-1, which signals to radio operators around the world, stopped working in just 21 days.
 
• **On 26 October 1957**, it stopped working due to its battery running out.
 
• The Sputnik 1 spacecraft was the first artificial satellite successfully placed in orbit around the Earth and was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome at Tyuratam (370 km southwest of the small town of Baikonur) in Kazakhstan, then part of the former Soviet Union.

questions.question: Kinetic and potential energies of a body are the components of its ______ energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mechanical.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The kinetic and potential energies of a body are the components of its mechanical energy.
 
• Mechanical Energy:
 
 
• The sum of potential energy and kinetic energy is called mechanical energy.
 
• From the above, it is clear that the total mechanical energy is the sum of potential energy and kinetic energy.
 
 

 
• **Potential Energy:**

 
 
• The energy of an object obtained by doing work against conservative forces like spring force and gravitational force is called potential energy.
 
• The potential energy of an object at a height from the ground is given as:
 
 
• **P = mgh**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• The energy obtained by an object by virtue of its motion is called kinetic energy.
 
 
• **KE = (1)/(2) times mv²**
 
 
 
• K is kinetic energy, v is the speed of the object, and m is the mass of the object.

questions.question: The first English factory was set up on the banks of the river ______ in 1651.
questions.solution:

• The first English factory was set up on the banks of the river **Hugli** in 1651.
 
• Hugli River is a Ganges River distributary, one of the many branches of the river that are collectively known as the** "Mouths of the Ganges."**
 
• The factory had a warehouse where goods for export were stored, and it had offices where Company officials sat.
 
• By 1696 it began building a fort around the settlement.
 
• Two years later it bribed Mughal officials into giving the Company zamindari rights over three villages.
 
• One of these was Kalikata, which later grew into the city of Calcutta, or Kolkata as it is known today.
 
• It also persuaded the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb to issue a 'Farman' granting the Company the right to trade duty-free.
 
• **'Farman'** means a royal edict or royal order.

questions.question: Who among the following has been the first sportsperson to receive the Padma Shri award from the Government of India?

• As of March 2021, he holds the Olympic record for most goals scored by an individual in an Olympic men's hockey final.

• 1952 Helsinki.
 
• 1956 Melbourne.

• He is known as The Flying Sikh and was an Indian track and field sprinter.

• He is the only athlete who won gold in 400 meters race at Asian Games & Games Commonwealth
 
• In 1957, Milkha Singh won the first National title in the 400 m race.
 
• He won gold medals in the 1958 and 1962 Asian Games.
 
• He also represented India in the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne, 1960 Summer Olympics in Rome, and 1964 Summer Olympics in Tokyo.
 
• **Milkha Singh was awarded the Padma Shri Medal in 1959**.
 
 
 
• **Dhanraj Pillay** is a retired field hockey player who played forward.
 
 
• He is also the former captain of the Indian National Hockey team.
 
• He is recorded to have scored 170 goals and for his contribution to the sport, he was awarded the Padma Shri in 2000.
 
 
 
• **Manpreet Singh Pawar **is an Indian hockey player and is also the captain of the Indian men’s national field hockey team since May 2017.
